correctness.rationale: PASS. Verified the geometric-fixed-space distinction after barycentric subdivision: an H-invariant chain has no rank-preserving nontrivial face permutation, hence every chain vertex is H-fixed. Such colored faces are exactly unions of H-vertex orbits with labels constant on H-edge orbits. Their restriction diagram is an inhabited flabby finite-set sheaf over a simplex; the published general inflation Theorems 5.1 and 5.3 apply and give the integral (c-1)-sphere wedge and homotopically Cohen–Macaulay structure. Counting cells with q^{e_H(J)} yields the signed subset-sum B_H(q). For g in N(H), the signed Lefschetz trace on fixed cells, with the sign of the permutation of each selected orbit block, gives the cycle-subset sum for top rational homology. Independent orbit reconstructions reproduce n=4, q=2 sphere counts C4:3, S4:1, double transposition:13, and the C5 normalizer multiplier-two reduced H0 trace 1. These finite examples do not prove all n,H; structural proof does.

originality.rationale: PASS. The strong general simplex-inflation theorem is openly cited as prior, as is the ambient S_n×S_q homology character. For cyclic H the latter can already imply a numerical Lefschetz/euler count and that count is not credited as original. The final result adds an explicit identification of actual geometric fixed spaces for arbitrary noncyclic H, their integral homotopy/CM type, and residual normalizer characters; the ambient representation alone does not give a normalizer representation on homology of every fixed locus. Mathematical implication comparison found no direct theorem covering these additional quantities; unindexed equivariant inflation results remain a priority risk.
